A1_verdict.alignment_theorem: If WGP2's transmission axis coincides with the detector axis, d^T J_WGP2(phi2) == t_perp2(nu) * d^T IDENTICALLY (J2 diagonal in that basis) -> a REAL WGP2 is mathematically indistinguishable from an IDEAL analyser times the scalar t_perp2(nu), for ANY E_in/theta/geometry. Verified to 4.4e-16 over 9 (psi,delta) combos; non-vacuous (10deg misalignment -> 6.1e-3 deviation).

Deficit direction: required extinction U(90)/U(0)=6.01e-5 (D_eff=4.683) vs 4.51e-3 (D_phys=11) -> data need the shadow 18.75 dB DEEPER, while misalignment scan (delta,psi<=20deg) only makes it SHALLOWER (up to +8.07 dB); 0/49 combos reach the target.

tasks.desc: OWNER PRIORITY QUESTION 2026-07-29 (out of order): is there a LINEARIZATION of Malus' law for a non-ideal polarizer with leakage? Answer + teaching note.
tasks.result: YES and it is EXACT, but the textbook 3-parameter form a0+a1cos2t+b1sin2t only holds for INTENSITY (incoherent) composition. For this project's COHERENT model (E=t_perp cos^2 + t_par sin^2, U=|E|^2) the exact linear basis is 5-dimensional: U = c0 + a2cos2t + b2sin2t + a4cos4t + b4sin4t (identity, synthetic resid rms 1.4e-16). Closed forms: |t_perp|^2=c0+c2+c4, |t_par|^2=c0-c2+c4, Re(t_perp conj(t_par))=c0-3c4 -> eta and cos(dphi) model-free; theta0=0.5*atan2(b2,a2) with ANALYTIC sigma (delta method), no multistart, no bootstrap. IDENTIFIABILITY: an angular scan at ONE frequency constrains at most 5 real numbers -> formal reason for the D_eff<->eta degeneracy. A4/A2 = 0.2498/0.2458/0.2549/0.2549 on data vs 0.25 exactly for ideal cos^4. *** KEY FOR A6: cost of ANGLES_LIMIT_2D=(0,90) measured — cond(XtX) 2.14 (full) vs 236.3 (truncated), sigma(theta0) 9.9x worse from PLAN GEOMETRY ALONE; theta0 shift full->truncated: 356att -0.687, series1 +0.351, series2 -2.103, test_grid -0.920 deg — COMPARABLE TO THE WHOLE A2 angle_offset dispute (-1.294/+0.219/+0.584). *** WEIGHTING MATTERS: unweighted LS on power weights points as U^2 -> blind to the shadow; series1 gave |t_par|^2<0. With sigma_i ~ U_i the two independent offsets (from h2 and h4) agree to 0.004-0.051 deg. Model-free theta0: +0.901+-0.184 / -0.546+-0.248 / -0.463+-0.198 / +0.599+-0.327 deg; eta 0.0127/0.0121/0.0130/0.0329 (M5 range 0.012-0.036). *** tau_leak model-free from slope of dphi(nu): 356att 0.195 ps vs M5's 0.19 ps (independent confirmation) but NOT universal (series2 -0.104 ps); reliability gated by Cauchy-Schwarz |cos dphi|<=1, violated 12/151, 43/94, 20/129, 0/147 -> OPEN QUESTION. Breaks linearity: log/dB scale, Fabry-Perot, detector nonlinearity, angle error. Does NOT break: eta(nu), phase term, Parseval summation, two-WGP structure (T8), phi2 misalignment.

Definition matches C's measurement: A = -10*lg[sum_nu|E(t1,t2,nu)|^2 / sum_nu|E(0,0,nu)|^2] (Parseval energy, normalised to the aligned config). API: attenuation_db, band_attenuation_db, attenuation_map, required_angle (inverse problem by bisection; explicit refusal + achievable max when the target is out of range). tasks.desc: Owner request: write the measurement protocol for scanning the beam across the aperture (THz + laser-pointer diffraction), so that the effect of lattice quality can be separated from the angular dependence.
tasks.result: Protocol written. Core idea: scan across the aperture at a FIXED angle — only the patch changes, which removes the angle/patch confounding of the existing data. Two-level design: (a) MAP — many positions x 4 angles (bright + theta_min-4/theta_min/theta_min+4); (b) ANCHORS — full angular sweeps at three positions (best zone, worst, transitional) so that M5 and the A0 harmonics give D_eff and eta PER ZONE. Optical diffraction scan first (seconds per frame vs minutes per THz trace) to choose the THz positions. Non-obvious but essential detail: three angles around the minimum are mandatory — U(theta) is quadratic at the minimum, so a local rotation of the wires (expected after re-tensioning) is otherwise indistinguishable from increased leakage; the parabola separates the floor (leakage) from the vertex (local wire orientation). Also: alignment step to put the beam ON the rotation axis (criterion: spot wanders < 0.5 mm over a full turn), hourly return to a reference position to scale drift against the zone effect, decision criterion fixed BEFORE measuring (spread of eta(x) must exceed the reference-repeat spread by >3x), and a filename convention purewave-x<XX>_<angle>deg_rep<N>_{sig,bg}.txt that makes each position its own dataset under DataManager's greedy parse — no code changes needed. Physical caveat recorded: a 1.5-2 mm waist is only 1-10 wavelengths across, so spatial resolution is frequency-dependent (0.2 THz averages over a much larger spot than 1.5 THz) and the focused beam carries a wide angular spectrum (P/cos effect on the effective period).

tasks.desc: Owner objected that the wire diameter must be smaller: at maximum magnification not all wires are in focus and the image smears out.
tasks.result: [ЧАСТИЧНО ОТОЗВАНО A16] Owner was right. Root cause: micrograph_period.in_focus_mask selects wires by QUANTILES WITHIN THE FRAME (top 45% by edge steepness, top 60% by brightness), which is a RELATIVE criterion - it always keeps about half the wires even when every one of them is blurred. Acceptable for a coplanar sample; wrong here, where the 0 / 0.12 mm focus pair shows the wires sit at different depths. New method: instead of deciding which wire is in focus, measure each wire's blur and bring them all to a common sharpness. Per wire: w10 = width at 10% of peak, b = blur = peak height / max |gradient| (inverse normalised edge steepness). Over 32 wires from 4 high-mag frames, r(w10, b) = +0.773, slope +0.211 um per px of blur. The reference sharpness is MEASURED, not chosen: the calibration graticule has physically sharp edges, so all blur seen there is instrumental - median 8.69 px = 1.10 um. Evaluating the regression there gives D = 10.91 +- 0.41 um (versus 9.08 +- 0.65 extrapolating to b -> 0, which over-corrects by removing the instrument PSF too, and 12.55 +- 0.60 uncorrected). Model-free corroboration: the single best wire of the 32 has w10 = 10.80 um, a hard upper bound consistent with 10.91. The owner's nominal 11 um is 0.8% away. KEY CONTROL: the same procedure on purewave gives slope +0.195 um/px against +0.211 here - 8% apart, so the blur-to-width relation is INSTRUMENTAL, not fitted to one sample. What differs is the blur spread: purewave 13-27 px versus 10-49 px here, five times wider, which is why purewave's correlation is weak (r = 0.21, narrow range) and this one's is strong. Consistent with purewave being a factory sample and nearly coplanar. CONSEQUENCE: D_eff is unchanged (refit confirms D_eff = 7.233, AIC -44783.7 identical - D_phys enters only the denominator and the seed), but D/P 0.395 -> 0.344, D_eff/D_phys 0.576 -> 0.663, H5 0.664 -> 0.708, deviation -0.088 -> -0.045, now inside the spread of the seven earlier samples. OPEN AND IMPORTANT: the same correction moves the reference too - purewave 10.6 -> 9.5 +- 2.1 - so every published diameter in the project carries a different amount of defocus. Either recompute D consistently across all samples with micrographs, which would also retune the empirical H5 law since it was fitted on those D/P, or state the incomparability explicitly. A blanket recomputation shifts the Phase 1-3 baseline and needs the owner's decision. || RETRACTION 2026-08-06 by A16: the value D = 10.91 does not survive scrutiny. The regression slope is inflated by the heavily defocused tail; restricted to weakly blurred wires it collapses to +0.16 for this sample. The stable estimator gives D = 12.60, i.e. the defocus correction is nearly zero in the working range. What stands from A14b: the diagnosis that in_focus_mask selects by within-frame quantiles and therefore does not remove blur as such, the per-wire blur metric itself, and the evidence of non-coplanarity.

tasks.desc: Recompute the wire diameter of every sample that has micrographs using the defocus correction of A14b, and re-derive the empirical H5 law from the corrected D/P.
tasks.result: H5 SURVIVED the uniform recomputation: k = 0.855 +- 0.085 over the four measured samples and 0.829 +- 0.040 over all eight (four of which keep passport geometry), against the previous 0.850. The reason for that stability matters more than the fact: D sits in both the numerator (D_eff/D_phys) and the denominator (D/P), so an error in D moves a point almost ALONG the law line - the law stability is weak evidence about D. THREE METHOD PROBLEMS were found and fixed. (1) The frame scale drifts: the pixel-period ratio high/mid must equal the calibration ratio 5.098 but measures 5.02/5.29/5.39/4.39, so a shared high-mag scale is invalid; every high-mag frame is now self-calibrated by the sample own period, which also makes D/P calibration-free. (2) The period was taken differently per sample (purewave mixed mid and high mag); now mid only, moving purewave 25.5 -> 24.72 um and forcing a refit, D_eff 6.982 -> 6.733. (3) Regressing width on blur OVER-CORRECTS - the r = 0.7-0.9 correlation comes from the heavily defocused tail, and restricted to weakly blurred wires the slope collapses to +0.47/+1.88/-0.34/+0.16, i.e. near best focus width barely depends on blur. THEREFORE A14b D = 10.91 IS WITHDRAWN; the stable estimator (median width over the sharpest quarter of wires, checked against thresholds 1.6-2.5 um) gives 12.60 for test_grid_33_11. FINAL GEOMETRY: purewave P 24.72 D 9.83 (D/P 0.398), specac 24.91 / 7.77 (0.312), test_grid_40_20 38.87 / 15.99 (0.411), test_grid_33_11 31.82 / 12.60 (0.396). The large diameter shifts are mostly NOT about defocus but about the old numbers coming from different estimators: specac 14.0 was a hand-applied ~x2 glint correction, not a measurement, and test_grid_40_20 18.0 was a measured 17 nudged toward the nominal 20. LIMITS: att-11-16 (4 of 8 points) cannot be measured at all - mid-mag frames only, wires nearly touching at D/P ~ 0.69, FFT returning 62/103/146 px instead of ~25 - so they keep passport geometry and yet they are what gives the eight-point fit its lever arm; the measured D/P range collapsed to 0.312-0.411 so the four-point slope carries a 10% error; test_grid_40_20 rests on three sharp wires; specac is internally inconsistent (our standard method gives 7.77 while even the under-reading glint estimate in the manifest was 8-12, and specac has the worst zoom mismatch at 14%) - NOT resolved; absolute D values are high by ~1.10 um of instrumental broadening. RECOMMENDATION: do not change the law.

methodology_notes: A2: angular add-on parameters in this problem are MULTIMODAL. Always warm-start nested variants from their submodel's optimum and run at least two starts (misalignment basin vs eps_cross basin); a cold start made phi2 look 16-sigma significant when the deeper basin puts it at 1.6+-4.8 (insignificant).

A3 SUPERSEDES the reading of the A2 note above: 'warm beats cold' is FALSE as a rule. Measured on M5_eps over 6 datasets x 2 angular ranges: 3-20 distinct basins per 21 starts, only 56/252 starts (22.2%) reach the global one, and cold wins 11 of 12 cases — but WHICH cold seed wins is dataset-dependent. The correct rule is a GRID of starts (|eps| x phase, plus several D_seed values, plus warm), then take the deepest basin and RECORD the gap. A2's own headline |eps_cross|=0.0345 came from the 4th-deepest basin of 11, 192.5 AIC above the global one.

A3: when a fitted parameter cluster is degenerate, check it against a MODEL-FREE estimator before interpreting it physically. Here the A0 harmonic eta is stable to x1.1-1.3 within an optical-configuration group while the M5 parameters (eta0, eps_cross, D_eff) that are supposed to encode the same physics wander by factors of 25-57 on the same data. The stable quantity is what may be reported; the decomposition is not.

A7: when a dataset is measured over several days, TEST THE STITCHING BEFORE FITTING. pi-periodicity of the transmission gives a model-free check at zero cost (theta and theta+180 are the same physical orientation) — here it exposed a x2.3 jump in leakage that a joint fit would have silently absorbed into eta0/eps_cross. Note also that ANGLES_LIMIT_2D=(0,90) can mix days without any warning.

A7: eta is reproducible WITHIN a mounting, not within a sample. The x2.3 shift between two days on the SAME polariser is comparable to the whole spread of eta between different samples — so leakage must be reported per measurement session, never as a sample constant.

A7/A9: ALWAYS ask how the sample is mounted before interpreting an angular scan. A narrow beam offset from the rotation axis makes angle and sample patch inseparable — the shadow and the bright channel then report on DIFFERENT pieces of the grid. This invalidated the first HN15 verdict within hours of writing it, and it retro-explains both the day-to-day eta jump on purewave and (possibly) the A6 asymmetry that no even-in-theta model term could absorb.
